# Mozambique

Wealth gradients in fertility and mortality: the values for an OG-Core calibration, followed by the estimates they are based on. Terms are defined in the [glossary](../glossary.md).

## Values for OG-Core

| OG-Core input | Wealth gradient | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `fert_gradient` | −1.11, by age as below | DHS 2022, TFR, plus [age offsets](../methods/fertility-by-age.md) |
| `infmort_gradient` | 0.09 | DHS 2022, infant mortality rate |
| `mort_gradient` | 1.64 − 0.302 × ln(GNI per capita) | [general gradient](../methods/general-gradient.md); for example −0.45 at $1,000 and −0.94 at $5,000, each with a 95% prediction interval of about ±0.4 |
| `imm_pctiles` | not provided | — |

Values are [wealth gradients](../glossary.md#wealth-gradient). Before they are passed to OG-Core, each is divided by 100 × (1 − p), where p is OG-Core's rate at that age ([details](../methods/ogcore-units.md)).

**Fertility gradient by age of mother** (`fert_gradient`; ages below 15 use the 15–19 value, ages 50 and above the 45–49 value):

| 15–19 | 20–24 | 25–29 | 30–34 | 35–39 | 40–44 | 45–49 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| −1.89 | −1.21 | −0.91 | −0.79 | −1.02 | −1.51 | −2.10 |

## Estimates

### Demographic and Health Surveys

Latest survey with a complete wealth-quintile breakdown ([`gradient_library_latest.csv`](../../data/gradient_library_latest.csv); earlier surveys in `gradient_library.csv`).

| Indicator | Survey | Lowest | Second | Middle | Fourth | Highest | Low/high ratio | Gradient |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Total fertility rate (births per woman) | 2022 | 6.8 | 6.3 | 5.3 | 4.3 | 2.7 | 2.52 | −1.11 |
| Infant mortality rate (per 1,000 live births) | 2022 | 34 | 38 | 46 | 43 | 35 | 0.97 | 0.09 |
| Under-five mortality rate (per 1,000 live births) | 2022 | 64 | 55 | 67 | 62 | 50 | 1.28 | −0.19 |

## Notes

- The 2007 census includes a household-deaths module but is not published. Compared with the deaths households report, the death records capture about 11 percent fewer deaths than average in the lowest wealth group, which would make the gradient too flat by about 0.15. Adult mortality therefore uses the general gradient.
